what_its_for: Olmesartan medoxomil is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). Lowering your blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems. It works by relaxing your blood vessels so your heart does not have to work as hard to pump blood.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with or without food, usually once a day. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time every day so it is easier to remember. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 20 mg once a day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 40 mg once a day if your blood pressure is not controlled after 2 weeks. For children ages 6 to 16 years, the dose is based on weight and will be decided by their doctor. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store olmesartan medoxomil tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C and 25°C). Keep the tablets in their original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from light, heat, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of any unused or expired medicine safely through a drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid using potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium without first talking to your doctor, as this medicine can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness or fainting. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position to reduce the risk of dizziness. Do not take non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) such as ibuprofen or naproxen without checking with your doctor, as they can make this medicine less effective and harm your kidneys.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience any of the following: swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of a serious allergic reaction called angioedema); severe dizziness or fainting; difficulty breathing; chest pain; signs of high potassium such as muscle weakness or irregular heartbeat; decreased urination or signs of kidney problems; or severe diarrhea and significant weight loss (a rare bowel condition called sprue-like enteropathy has been reported with long-term use).
when_it_works: Olmesartan starts to lower your blood pressure within 1 to 2 hours after you take your first dose. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit of this medicine. Keep taking it even if you feel well, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Do NOT take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. It can seriously harm or even cause death to an unborn baby, especially during the second and third trimesters. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant while taking this medicine. Breastfeeding: It is not known if this medicine passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: This medicine can be used in children 6 years and older for high blood pressure, with doses based on weight. It is not recommended for children under 6 years old or for children with certain kidney conditions. Elderly patients: Older adults may be more sensitive to the blood pressure-lowering effects of this medicine and may be at higher risk of dizziness and falls. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
